source: Case002 original screenplay and storyboard; Z02 zero-evacuee replacement, one new rendering in a separate author turn after rejecting gender-assumptive Z02.

scenes.focus: a serious dark-haired woman newspaper editor inspects a newly printed broadsheet with two distinct columns of dense newspaper type, standing close beside an old heavy printing press during the first daylight hours
scenes.camera: intimate medium vertical view from behind and slightly over the editor's shoulder, emphasizing the single printed page in both hands, the cast-iron press, and her pinned-up dark hair; no full face or other character visible
scenes.location: a compact soot-stained Birmingham newspaper printing room in the 1920s
required: one woman newspaper editor with dark hair pinned up, rolled cream blouse sleeves and dark period waistcoat holding a fresh broadsheet in both hands
one full broadsheet displaying two separate dense columns of small indistinct period newspaper print, without a legible personal name or headline
one large worn cast-iron newspaper letterpress with ink-dark rollers and stacked news sheets on a wooden bench
scenes.background: letterpress type racks, inking pot and rags, soot-dark old brick walls, rain-dimmed tall workshop window and industrial chimney silhouettes beyond
scenes.light: early cool grey daylight through the printing-room window with a warm amber gas lamp grazing the press metal and paper fibers
scenes.npc: Nora, the serious dark-haired newspaper editor, seen from the back or hidden three-quarter profile; no visible witness faces, no identifiable playable detective
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: The finished printed page may represent publication of two independently checked chains of evidence in this particular ending. No real witness names, home addresses or a child's identity may be read. The image does not specify which two or three witnesses are protected and does not imply that Vale has been convicted, that Mercer testified, or that justice is complete. Those details belong to the actual story state and narrative overlay.
avoid: real or invented legible witness names, identifying signatures, private addresses, child's details or sensational accusation headline
Vale in custody, a police verdict, courtroom conviction, or a crowd celebrating a completed prosecution
three people shown as universally rescued when their individual witness statuses can vary
recognizable faces of the five selectable heroes or a substitute canonical face for Nora

scenes.focus: a solitary black leather-gloved hand in the close foreground holds one closed worn brown document folio near the open doorway of an empty dark red passenger train at dawn, while the deserted rain-soaked platform stretches toward Birmingham's smoke stacks
scenes.camera: first-person close view angled toward the carriage's empty entrance and iron step, with only the lower edge of one black glove and the plain folio in the foreground, no visible body or face
scenes.location: a rain-wet railway platform outside industrial Birmingham in the 1920s
required: one black leather-gloved hand alone at the bottom of the scene holding one fully closed weathered brown document folio with a brass clasp
a stationary old dark burgundy riveted railway carriage with open doorway, empty amber-lit compartment and wet iron boarding step
a deserted stone platform with empty benches, vintage station lanterns and distant smoky factory chimneys in pale morning light
scenes.background: a cast-iron platform canopy, reflective puddles on old stone pavement, dark brick railway buildings and smoke-dimmed industrial rooftops
scenes.light: soft grey-orange dawn behind the chimneys and amber gas-lamp glow inside the empty carriage reflecting across the wet platform
scenes.npc: only a small cropped anonymous gloved hand is present; no full silhouette, head, face, body or other person appears
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: Only the zero-evacuee ending state is represented: the investigator departs with the closed folio but no witness is shown or implied to have been evacuated. The hand does not identify any playable hero by gender, appearance or body shape. Routes with evacuated witnesses require their own state-appropriate artwork or separately verified neutral coverage.
avoid: a visible male or female protagonist, full body, shoulders, face, cap or recognizable hero silhouette
any protected or evacuated witness waiting on the platform or inside the carriage
a visible new identity, readable document, name, station label or confirmed outcome for absent witnesses
a crowd, safe-house arrival, triumphant rescue or guarantee that all witnesses are protected
